name: toolsmith-text-replace
intent: Replace exact, literal text in existing files as one all-or-nothing change.
use_when: You would otherwise write a Python, Ruby, sed or perl script to find text in a file and replace it.
You need several edits in one or more files in one call, and every edit must match before any file changes.
You want to delete whole lines, or change text inside a long line, by quoting it exactly.
not_for: Creating a new file: use the Write tool.
Pattern-based changes (regular expressions, captures): this tool matches literal text only.
A single small edit you can make with the Edit tool just as easily.
Binary files, or files with CRLF line endings.
input:
An edit spec on stdin, in blocks. Each block starts with a header line:

    @@ <path> [--all | --count N]

The path is relative to the current directory and has no spaces. After the header come one or more edits. An edit is one or more '-' lines (the text to find) followed by zero or more '+' lines (the text to put in its place). The text after the '-' or '+' is taken exactly, spaces included; the lines of an edit are joined with newlines. A new '-' line after '+' lines starts the next edit in the same file.

- Matching is literal and may start or end mid-line, like the Edit tool.
- By default each edit must match exactly once. --all replaces every match (at least one); --count N requires exactly N matches. The option applies to every edit in the block.
- Edits apply in order, so a later edit sees the result of an earlier one. Several blocks may name the same file.
- To delete whole lines, end the '-' lines with a '-' alone (that adds the final newline) and give no '+' lines.
- A '-' or '+' alone is an empty line of text. Empty spec lines may separate edits and blocks, never sit inside one.
- Every line of the spec starts with '@@', '-' or '+', or is empty.

options.text: Check every edit and print the changes, but write nothing.

output: On success, stdout shows each edit as 'path:line' with the whole changed lines before ('- ') and after ('+ '), then 'Done: N replacements in M files.' For --all or --count, all match lines are listed and the first change is shown. Files are written only after every edit matched, each through a temporary file that is renamed over the original, keeping its permissions. On failure, nothing is written and stderr names each failed edit with its spec line, the match count, and the closest text in the file: where a multi-line match breaks, or the most similar lines.

exit_codes.text: Every edit matched and was applied (or, with --dry-run, would be).
Nothing written: an edit matched the wrong number of times, or a file could not be read.
Nothing written: the spec or the arguments are wrong.
A write failed after other files were written; the message lists the files already written.

examples.title: One edit in one file
examples.stdout:
config/app.yml:2
- port: 3000
+ port: 4000
Done: 1 replacement in 1 file.

examples.title: Several edits in two files: a multi-line match, every match with --all, and a whole-line deletion
examples.stdin:
@@ app/models/hub.rb
-  attr_reader :key, :intro
+  attr_reader :key, :intro, :tagline
-    @intro = intro
-  end
+    @intro = intro
+    @tagline = nil
+  end

@@ docs/api.md --all
-blog_api.token
+api.token

@@ docs/api.md
-Legacy: yes
-
examples.stdout:
app/models/hub.rb:2
-   attr_reader :key, :intro
+   attr_reader :key, :intro, :tagline
app/models/hub.rb:6
-     @intro = intro
-   end
+     @intro = intro
+     @tagline = nil
+   end
docs/api.md:1,3 (2 replacements, first shown)
- Token: `blog_api.token`
+ Token: `api.token`
docs/api.md:2
- Legacy: yes
Done: 5 replacements in 2 files.

examples.title: Dry run: check and show, write nothing
examples.stdout:
README.md:1
- Run bin/setup first.
+ Run bin/dev first.
Dry run: 1 replacement in 1 file would be made; nothing written.

examples.title: One edit does not match, so nothing is written
examples.stdin:
@@ b.rb
-x = 1
+x = 2

@@ a.rb
-def total
-  items.sum(:price)
+def total
+  items.sum(&:cost)
examples.stderr:
toolsmith-text-replace: nothing written: 1 of 2 edits failed.

a.rb (spec line 6): found 0 matches, expected 1.
  The first '-' line matches file line 1, but the text differs at file line 2:
    file line 2: |  items.sum(&:price)|
    '-' line 2:  |  items.sum(:price)|

examples.title: A match that is not unique
examples.stderr:
toolsmith-text-replace: nothing written: 1 of 1 edit failed.

list.txt (spec line 2): found 2 matches (lines 1, 3), expected 1.
  Add surrounding text to the '-' lines to make the match unique, or put --all or --count 2 on the '@@' line.
